A soap molecule is the sodium salt of a long-chain carboxylic acid with two ends: a hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail that dissolves in oil and grease, and a hydrophilic ionic head that dissolves in water.
Micelle action: tails dig into oily dirt while heads stay in water; agitation forms spherical micelles with the oil trapped inside, and rinsing water carries the whole micelle away.
Soap fails in hard water because Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions form insoluble scum with it; detergents, being sulphonate or ammonium salts of long-chain acids, stay effective in hard water.
Common exam mistake: swapping tail and head roles; the tail hides in dirt, the head faces water, and a micelle forms only around oily dirt.

keyTerms.meaning: Sweet-smelling compound formed by reaction of an acid with an alcohol, used in perfumes.
Reaction of an ester with NaOH to give alcohol and the sodium salt of the acid, the basis of soap making.
Spherical cluster formed by soap molecules around oily dirt with tails inward and heads outward in water.

sections.trick: Soap is two-faced: TAIL Toward grime, HEAD Toward H2O; the micelle simply wraps the grease into a rinse-able ball.
sections.examPointer: Case studies show the esterification test tube (sweet fruity smell) or soap lather failing in hard water; keep both equations and the scum reason (calcium and magnesium salts) ready.

mcqs.question: The number of covalent bonds present in an ethane molecule (C2H6) is
mcqs.explanation: Ethane has 6 C-H bonds and 1 C-C bond, making 7 covalent bonds in total.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
mcqs.explanation: C2H4 contains a carbon-carbon double bond, so it is unsaturated; the others have only single bonds.

mcqs.question: The functional group present in CH3COOH is
mcqs.explanation: The -COOH ending of CH3COOH is the carboxylic acid functional group.

mcqs.question: The next higher homologue of ethanol (C2H5OH) is
mcqs.explanation: Successive homologues differ by CH2, so the next higher alcohol after C2H5OH is C3H7OH (propanol).

mcqs.question: Vegetable oils are converted into vanaspati ghee by
options: Addition of hydrogen using a nickel catalyst
mcqs.explanation: Hydrogenation adds hydrogen to unsaturated oils in the presence of a nickel catalyst, giving saturated vanaspati ghee.

mcqs.question: The reaction of an ester with sodium hydroxide is called
mcqs.explanation: Heating an ester with NaOH splits it into alcohol and the sodium salt of the acid; this soap-making reaction is saponification.

mcqs.question: Which property of graphite makes it suitable as an electrode material in dry cells?
options: Presence of free electrons that conduct electricity
mcqs.explanation: Graphite conducts electricity due to free electrons, which makes it useful as electrode material.

mcqs.question: When ethanol reacts with sodium metal, the gas evolved is
mcqs.explanation: Ethanol reacts with sodium to give sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas, which burns with a pop sound.

mcqs.question: How many structural isomers are possible for butane (C4H10)?
mcqs.explanation: Butane C4H10 exists as two structural isomers, n-butane and isobutane, due to different chain arrangements.

mcqs.question: Which compound gives brisk effervescence with sodium bicarbonate solution?
mcqs.explanation: Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium bicarbonate releasing brisk effervescence of CO2; ethanol, ethanal and ethene do not.

boardQuestions.question: Why does carbon form compounds mainly by covalent bonding? State the two key properties of carbon that lead to a very large number of carbon compounds.
boardQuestions.answer: 1) Carbon has four electrons in its outermost shell; gaining or losing four electrons would require very large energy, so carbon shares electrons to complete its octet, forming covalent bonds. 2) Tetravalency lets each carbon bond with four other atoms, including hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, halogens and other carbons. 3) Catenation allows carbon atoms to link into straight chains, branched chains and rings, and C-C bonds are strong and stable, so millions of compounds become possible.

boardQuestions.question: Why is the conversion of ethanol into ethanoic acid called an oxidation reaction? Write the equation involved and name the oxidising agents used.
boardQuestions.answer: 1) Ethanol, C2H5OH, on heating with alkaline KMnO4 or acidified K2Cr2O7 changes to ethanoic acid: C2H5OH + 2(O) -> CH3COOH + H2O. 2) In this change oxygen is added to the compound and the hydrogen content decreases, which is exactly the definition of oxidation. 3) Since the oxidising agent supplies the oxygen and gets reduced itself, ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid; alkaline KMnO4 and acidified K2Cr2O7 are the two oxidising agents used.

boardQuestions.question: Describe the bonding in diamond and graphite and explain why graphite conducts electricity while diamond does not.
boardQuestions.answer: 1) In diamond, each carbon atom is bonded to four other carbon atoms by strong covalent bonds in a rigid three-dimensional network, so diamond is extremely hard and has a very high melting point. 2) Since every outer electron of carbon is used in bonding, diamond has no free electrons and therefore does not conduct electricity. 3) In graphite, each carbon is bonded to only three other carbons forming flat hexagonal layers; the fourth electron of each carbon is free, which lets graphite conduct electricity, while the weak forces between layers allow them to slide, making graphite soft and slippery.

boardQuestions.question: What is a homologous series? Write the general formulas of alkanes, alkenes and alkynes and state how successive members differ from each other.
boardQuestions.answer: 1) A homologous series is a family of carbon compounds having the same general formula, the same functional group and similar chemical properties, where each successive member differs from the previous one by a CH2 unit, adding 14 u to the molecular mass. 2) General formulas: alkanes CnH2n+2 (methane CH4, ethane C2H6), alkenes CnH2n (ethene C2H4) and alkynes CnH2n-2 (ethyne C2H2). 3) Example of one series: alcohols CH3OH, C2H5OH and C3H7OH, where properties such as the reaction with sodium repeat across members while melting and boiling points rise gradually. 4) A quick membership check: confirm two things, the repeating CH2 difference and the unchanged functional group; when both hold, the compounds belong to one homologous family.

boardQuestions.question: Explain four chemical properties of carbon compounds with balanced equations: (i) combustion, (ii) oxidation of ethanol, (iii) addition reaction (hydrogenation), (iv) substitution reaction (chlorination of methane). Mention one use of each in daily life.
boardQuestions.answer: 1) Combustion: carbon compounds burn in oxygen to give carbon dioxide, water, heat and light, for example CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O + heat; this property makes hydrocarbons like LPG and CNG valuable household fuels. 2) Oxidation: alcohols are oxidised to carboxylic acids by alkaline KMnO4 or acidified K2Cr2O7 on heating: C2H5OH + 2(O) ->(alkaline KMnO4, heat) CH3COOH + H2O; controlled oxidation gives ethanoic acid used in food and industry. 3) Addition reaction: unsaturated hydrocarbons add hydrogen across multiple bonds in the presence of a nickel or palladium catalyst: C2H4 + H2 ->(Ni catalyst) C2H6; hydrogenation converts liquid vegetable oils into saturated vanaspati ghee. 4) Substitution reaction: in saturated hydrocarbons, hydrogen is replaced stepwise by chlorine in sunlight: CH4 + Cl2 ->(sunlight) CH3Cl + HCl, followed by CH3Cl + Cl2 -> CH2Cl2 + HCl; such substituted products serve as solvents and refrigerants in industry. 5) Key contrast: saturated compounds mainly undergo substitution and give a clean flame, while unsaturated compounds mainly undergo addition and give a sooty yellow flame. 6) Writing tip: for each reaction, put the reagent or catalyst above the arrow, name the organic product, and end with one daily-life line, because these three tags carry the structure marks in the scheme.

boardQuestions.question: Describe the structure of a soap molecule and explain the cleansing action of soap through micelle formation. Why does soap fail in hard water, and what alternative is used?
boardQuestions.answer: 1) A soap molecule is the sodium salt of a long-chain carboxylic acid and has two ends: a long hydrocarbon chain called the tail, which is hydrophobic and mixes only with oil and grease, and an ionic carboxylate head, which is hydrophilic and dissolves in water. 2) Cleansing action: when soap is rubbed on an oily cloth, the hydrophobic tails of many molecules dig into the oily dirt while the hydrophilic heads remain in water; on agitation, the dirt gets wrapped inside spherical micelles with tails inward and heads outward. 3) Because the outside of each micelle is water-loving, rinsing with water carries the entire oil-filled micelle away, leaving the cloth clean; the lather helps spread the soap and lift the dirt. 4) Failure in hard water: calcium and magnesium ions of hard water react with soap to form an insoluble scum (calcium and magnesium salts of the fatty acid), so lather does not form and soap is wasted. 5) Remedy: detergents, which are sulphonate or ammonium salts of long-chain acids; their charged heads do not precipitate with hard-water ions, so they work in hard water, though some detergents are not easily biodegradable and can pollute water. 6) One-line revision summary: soap wraps grease in water-friendly packages, hard water steals the soap into scum, and detergents dodge that theft.

boardQuestions.question: CASE: A student mixed 2 mL of ethanol with 2 mL of ethanoic acid in a test tube and added a few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid. The tube was kept in a beaker of warm water (a water bath) for about five minutes, and a pleasant fruity smell came from the tube. (a) Name the reaction and write the balanced chemical equation for it. (b) What is the role of concentrated sulphuric acid, and why was a water bath used instead of a direct flame? (c) What would happen if the product is heated with sodium hydroxide solution? Write the equation and name the reaction.
boardQuestions.answer: 1) (a) The reaction is esterification: CH3COOH + C2H5OH ->(conc. H2SO4) CH3COOC2H5 + H2O; the pleasant fruity smell is that of the ester ethyl ethanoate formed when ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol. 2) (b) Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a catalyst and also as a dehydrating agent, absorbing the water formed so that the reversible reaction moves forward and more ester is produced. 3) (b) A water bath is used because the mixture contains ethanol, which is highly inflammable, so gentle and uniform heating is safer than a direct burner flame. 4) (c) On heating the ester with sodium hydroxide solution, it splits back into the alcohol and the sodium salt of the acid: CH3COOC2H5 + NaOH -> CH3COONa + C2H5OH; this reaction is saponification, the same process used industrially when fats and oils are boiled with NaOH to produce soap. 5) Conclusion: the pair of reactions shows that ester formation and ester breaking are reversible chemical partners, and quoting both equations with the catalyst and conditions noted fetches full marks. 6) Observation note: the fruity smell appears only after gentle warming, because at room temperature the reversible reaction is too slow to make enough ester for the smell to be noticed.
